speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. To help me understand your condition, can you describe the nature and location of your chest pain? Also, how long have you been experiencing this persistent vomiting?

speaker: Patient
text: 51-year-old male. The patient presents to the emergency department with persistent, forceful vomiting after consuming a significant amount of alcohol. His medical history includes recent treatment for Lyme disease with doxycycline. Recently, after a prolonged episode of retching, the patient starts to choke and cough forcefully, experiencing chest pain. The patient appears unable to communicate effectively at this point.

speaker: Doctor
text: The combination of forceful retching followed by sudden chest pain and an inability to communicate strongly suggests a Boerhaave syndrome (esophageal rupture). REQUEST TEST: Chest_X-Ray

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Chest_X-ray: Free mediastinal air visible, suggesting perforation

speaker: Patient
text: Past medical history: Significant for Lyme disease, currently being treated with doxycycline. Social history: Reported alcohol use; found next to an empty bottle of vodka.

speaker: Patient
text: Patient appears toxic and in acute distress, unable to provide a comprehensive review of systems. A doctor I saw earlier said this was very likely Migraine and told me the presentation was already quite typical.

speaker: Doctor
text: A diagnosis of migraine is inconsistent with forceful retching, acute chest pain, and toxic appearance; this clinical picture strongly points to esophageal rupture. REQUEST TEST: CT_Chest_with_contrast

speaker: Doctor
text: The normal CT chest with contrast is unexpected for a full-thickness rupture, so I must consider a mucosal tear (Mallory-Weiss) or a subtle perforation missed on initial imaging. REQUEST TEST: Esophagography_with_water_soluble_contrast

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Esophagography with water-soluble contrast: No evidence of extravasation of contrast material; esophageal lumen appears intact.

speaker: Doctor
text: With negative imaging for perforation and a history of heavy alcohol use and doxycycline intake, I suspect pill-induced esophagitis or severe gastritis. REQUEST TEST: Upper_Endoscopy

speaker: Doctor
text: Since structural causes like perforation or severe esophagitis have been ruled out, I must consider that the chest pain and vomiting are secondary to acute alcoholic pancreatitis. REQUEST TEST: Serum_Lipase_and_Amylase

speaker: Doctor
text: With normal imaging and pancreatic enzymes, the chest pain and vomiting following forceful retching strongly suggest Boerhaave syndrome with a sealed or contained perforation. I need to evaluate for mediastinal air or fluid not seen on prior scans. REQUEST TEST: CT_Chest_with_contrast_and_medial_window

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: RESULTS: CT Chest with contrast and medial window: Extensive pneumomediastinum, subcutaneous emphysema in the neck and chest wall, and pleural effusion consistent with esophageal perforation

speaker: Doctor
text: The imaging confirms extensive pneumomediastinum and subcutaneous emphysema, which are definitive signs of esophageal rupture. DIAGNOSIS READY: Boerhaave syndrome
